title: 1-Bit Half Adder Circuit
summary: A Half Adder is a combinational logic circuit that adds two 1-bit binary digits (A and B). It produces two outputs: Sum (S) and Carry (C).

images.title: Block Diagram
images.caption: 1-Bit Half Adder Functional Block Diagram with Inputs A, B and Outputs Sum, Carry.

images.title: Gate-Level Schematic
images.caption: Half Adder constructed using 1 XOR gate (IC 7486) and 1 AND gate (IC 7408).

images.title: Breadboard Wiring Diagram
images.caption: Wiring IC 7486 and IC 7408 on breadboard to form Half Adder.

working_principle: Binary addition operates as follows: 0+0=0, 0+1=1, 1+0=1, and 1+1=10 (Sum=0, Carry=1). The Sum output matches an XOR operation (A ⊕ B), while the Carry output matches an AND operation (A · B).
boolean_equation: Sum = A ⊕ B,  Carry = A · B
applications: ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) LSB addition stage
Address Generation Units in Memory Controllers
advantages: Can be synthesized using 5 NAND gates (IC 7400) or 5 NOR gates (IC 7402)
disadvantages: Does NOT accept a Carry-In from a previous stage (Requires a Full Adder for multi-bit addition)
common_mistakes: Attempting to cascade Half Adders for multi-bit addition without Carry-In logic.
Connecting Sum output to Carry pin by mistake.
quick_notes: Requires 5 NAND gates to build using Universal Gates.

viva_questions.q: What are the Boolean equations for Sum and Carry in a Half Adder?
viva_questions.a: Sum = A ⊕ B, Carry = A · B.

viva_questions.q: Why is it called a 'Half' Adder?
viva_questions.a: Because it only adds two 1-bit inputs and cannot accept a Carry-In bit from a lower order stage.

interview_questions.q: How many NAND gates are required to construct a Half Adder?
How do you form a Full Adder using two Half Adders?
interview_questions.a: Connect the Sum output of the first Half Adder to the input of the second Half Adder along with Cin, and OR the Carry outputs of both Half Adders.
